Ari — thanks for the details, and congrats on the Q3 timeline. We can absolutely support a us-east primary pool with an eu-west fallback; the exact configuration depends on expected cross-region failover RTO/RPO and how you want traffic routed during normal operation.

Quick answers up front:
- Provisioning: yes — we’ll provision a dedicated GPU pool in us-east and can register a smaller eu-west standby pool that receives <5% traffic under normal ops, and absorbs traffic on failover.
- Burst policy: we typically implement a two-tier burst window — a short, high-throughput fast-burst (1–10 minutes) with strict token quotas and a longer soft-burst (up to 1 hour) that applies graceful degradation rules.

To prepare the SOW and capacity matrix I need:
1) Typical token length per request (or median/95th if you have it).
2) Expected sustained concurrency during peak (you gave rps; concurrency helps sizing).
3) Any regulatory constraints for eu-west (PII routing, key management).

Proposed next steps:
- Quick 30m sync Thursday 10:30 PT to confirm traffic profile and sign off on provisional sizing.
- We’ll produce a draft SOW and a region_capacity_matrix.csv that maps pool sizes to expected latency and cost estimates.

I’ve attached a short pre-provision checklist — please have your infra/security folks scan it before the call. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Internal note — Ari’s numbers look reasonable. Quick ops thoughts before the customer call:

- US-east inventory: we have two spare multi-GPU racks that can be carved into a dedicated pool at the sizes they’re requesting; lead time ~6 business days for reservation and network prep.
- EU-west: recommend a minimal standby pool (1–2 machines) with cross-region KV-replication disabled by default — we’ll only enable RW state replication if they need sub-minute failover.
- Burst policy constraints: to keep cost predictable we should offer a capped fast-burst token bucket (e.g., allow 10x for up to 5 minutes, then enforce 50% throttling for 15 minutes) and present an option for a paid longer burst window.

Action items for us before the call:
1) Monica — produce a region_capacity_matrix mapping 50/120/300 rps to pool sizes and cost.
2) Vivek — confirm us-east rack reservation availability and any AZ affinity concerns.
3) Jordan — capture customer answers during kickoff and lock the recommended profile into the SOW.
